result: Systematic review of 18 physiotherapy RCTs (3 CF, 14 CFS, 1 PEM-required ME): intervention effects, if any, disappeared with narrower PEM-based case definitions, more objective outcomes and longer follow-up; no evidence of effective physiotherapy for ME.
reason: Paper is about the GET/exercise-trial evidence base (criteria, objective outcomes, follow-up), matching the PACE/GET finding; it reports no measured harm rates, so it does not test the NICE-harms worsening claim directly.

result: Teesside thesis: meta-analysis of 32 cross-sectional studies found pooled VO2peak 5.2 ml/kg/min (95% CI 3.8-6.6) lower in ME/CFS than healthy controls.
reason: already cited (thesis version of the Franklin 2018/2021 Teesside meta-analysis, same pooled 5.2 ml/kg/min)

result: Meta-analysis of 37 studies (1016 patients, 686 controls): RPE during acute aerobic exercise was higher in ME/CFS and FM than controls (Hedges d 0.85, 95% CI 0.62-1.08).
reason: Measures perceived exertion during exercise, not EEfRT effort-based choice; no atlas finding covers RPE (could be a new item in the exertion domain).

result: Post hoc analysis of the Phase III rintatolimod trial (ITT n=208): in 2-8 years' illness (n=75) placebo-adjusted treadmill gains were over twice the ITT effect and 51.2% improved exercise duration by 25% or more (p=0.003); no response in >8 years (n=133).
reason: already cited (Strayer 2020, PLoS One post hoc)

result: In 100 severe ME/CFS vs 15 controls, sitting for an hour lowered extracranial Doppler CBF (474 vs 627 mL/min; mean decline 24.5%, -26.9% in the 90 with OI symptoms), larger with prior POTS (28.8% vs 22.3%); supine CBF normal.
reason: Same group and method, distinct paper from the cited 429-patient tilt study; extends to severe patients with a sitting stressor and reproduces the size of the fall.

result: In 100 severe ME/CFS vs 15 controls, sitting for an hour lowered extracranial Doppler CBF (474 vs 627 mL/min; mean decline 24.5%, -26.9% in the 90 with OI symptoms), larger with prior POTS (28.8% vs 22.3%); supine CBF normal.
reason: Same measure (extracranial Doppler CBF under orthostatic stress), extends to severe bed-bound patients using sitting; not one of the listed van Campen papers.

result: In 248 ME/CFS (164 with FM) vs 22 controls, pressure pain thresholds fell after head-up tilt in patients with and without FM but not in controls; windup was higher than controls before and after tilt, unchanged by tilt.
reason: Same measures (PPT, temporal summation) and same post-stressor threshold fall, extended from exercise to orthostatic stress, with FM stratification.

result: Systematic review of sMRI/fMRI studies to April 2019: structural differences (grey/white matter volume, ventricles, hyperintensities) were inconsistent, with three studies finding none; most consistent fMRI finding was increased activation and extra region recruitment; no biomarker.
reason: A second systematic review reaching the same conclusion as Shan 2020 (inconsistent structural findings), though with heavily overlapping primary studies.

result: Systematic review of sMRI/fMRI studies to April 2019: structural differences inconsistent; task fMRI most consistently showed increased activation and extra region recruitment; no biomarker.
reason: Abstract covers task-based fMRI only, not resting-state connectivity; the task-fMRI point is already captured via the neuro-mri-structure link.

result: In 289 ME/CFS patients graded by ICC severity (121 mild, 98 moderate, 70 severe), SF-36 physical function (70/43/15), steps/day (8235/5195/2031), %predicted VO2 at ventilatory threshold (47/38/30%) and %predicted peak VO2 (90/64/48%) all fell with severity (all significant).
reason: Does not measure prevalence of severe illness or treatment response; it adds a severity gradient for peak VO2 (no control group), extending the low peak VO2 finding.
